(This evening through next Wednesday)

WEATHER PATTERN OVERVIEW: 

The first of several pieces of energy has moved through NV 
bringing snow across much of the area as temperatures came in 
below forecast last night. Overall forecast is still on track as 
the next piece of energy is making its way over the Sierra’s and 
into western Nevada. This afternoon snow or a rain snow mix is 
taking place along I 80 and US 95 corridors as eastern Nevada 
enjoyed a brief pause in precipitation this morning. Transition to
all snow will again take place this evening quickly after sunset,
as the loss of any heating helps amplify the wet-bulb cooling 
effect. Accumulation totals for this part will be likely be 
similar to Wednesday nights event for most with the lower 
elevation valleys seeing between 0.5” up to 3”, higher elevation 
valleys could see between 2” to 4” of new snow. For passes and 
road summits snow 3” to 5” of new snowfall, with the mountain 
ranges seeing all snow with this event with totals between 8” to 
18” plus possible. Winds are still going to be elevated through 
the rest of the evening, as gusty S to SW winds will be possible 
through Friday morning. Especially for central Nevada as N Nye, 
White Pine, southern Lander, and S Eureka Counties could see South
to Southwest winds of 20 to 30 MPH with gusts up to 40 MPH 
possible. Further north winds aren’t expected to be as strong, but
will still be breezy at 15 to 25 MPH with gust up to 35 MPH 
possible. The combination of winds and snowfall will bring adverse
to hazardous driving conditions for area highways Thursday 
evening through Friday. Winter headlines continue for area with a 
Winter Storm Warning for the Ruby Mountains, and a winter Weather 
Advisory for Parts of Elko, Eureka, Lander, Humboldt, and White 
Pine Counties through Friday evening. Friday a cold front will 
push through the region which will shift wind to the NW with 
breezy conditions continuing with speeds of 10 to 20 MPH with 
gusts up the 30 MPH possible. Also for Friday the main upper 
trough will pass overhead, and with that will be the possibility 
for isolated to scattered convective snow showers and snow squalls
which would offer less overall precipitation coverage, but give 
enhanced precipitation rates. These event could bring a boost to 
local snow totals. Central Nevada will see the greatest chances 
for these features as instability, what little there is will be 
concentrated along the US 50 corridor. Temperatures for this event
will likely depend on precipitation mechanics as areas with 
active precipitation will be cooler due to wet bulb effects, only 
to rebound as breaks in precipitation occur. Overall highs will 
range in the low 30s to low 40s with lows in the upper 20s through
Saturday morning. With the exit of this upper trough, Saturday 
will see a brief break as a short wave ridge passes through. This 
break however will be short lived as another upper level trough 
will start to move through Sunday afternoon through Monday 
evening. This system looks to be weaker and faster than Thursdays 
storm, but could have the potential to bring isolated rain/snow 
showers with accumulations of 0.5” to 2” of snow for the passes 
and range summits, and up to 0.10” of rain for the valleys. 
Tuesday will bring another quick break in the action before 
another system will try to move through for next Wednesday with 
more chances for rain/snow showers. Temperature for the rest of 
the week look to remain near to or below normal as highs look to 
range in the upper 30s to upper 40s with lows in the upper teens 
to 20s for overnight lows. 


FORECAST CONFIDENCE & DEVIATIONS: 
 
There is high confidence in winter precipitation and breezy to 
gusty winds Today and Friday with parts of NE Nevada.

There is medium confidence for another, weaker upper level trough
passage across Nevada Sunday and Monday. 

There is medium confidence of a third upper trough pushing into 
the western US for next Wednesday.
